checks: A nonzero nullspace force gives a linear ray to minus infinity. In its absence completion of the square on the range gives the value and the full affine set of minimizers.
Minimizing the quartic model by the nonnegative variable theta squared gives zero on one side and minus h squared over four on the other. The one-sided second derivatives differ.
The positive-definite substitution reduces a feasible constraint with redundant rows to a minimum-norm solution. The range of the row map equals the range of its Gram matrix.
Source 0e4cb84a76d46e82 §2 includes both the singular model and the independent positive-definite incidence constraint.

overlap.comparison: Uses a strict scalar threshold optimum. It does not supply either the singular-kernel alternative or the redundant linear constraint formula.

readability: The definitions, scope, and proof order are clear.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The singular quadratic criterion and constrained extra cost are exact. The quartic example correctly limits any implication for a genuinely optimized value.
